item.title: US Stock Futures Up Ahead of Talks, Dollar Steady: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures edged higher, while the dollar held in a narrow range as traders awaited US-China talks ahead of a leaders summit later this week.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess

item.title: AI Boom Is Making Diversifying Investments Tough for Wall Street
item.description: Pensions and sovereign wealth funds with many billions to invest are finding the diversification they once relied on is an illusion.
item.dc:creator: Lu Wang

item.title: Short-Term Treasuries Emerge as Popular Bet on Fed Inflation Win
item.description: Investors in the US Treasury market are shifting their focus to owning shorter-dated government bonds, a bet that the Federal Reserve will eventually emerge victorious in its fight against inflation.
item.dc:creator: Michael MacKenzie and Ye Xie

item.title: QatarEnergy on Energy Security and Supply
item.description: H.E. Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, Minister of State for Energy Affairs for the State of Qatar and President & CEO of QatarEnergy discusses how geopolitics, energy security and investment are reshaping global energy markets with Bloomberg’s Annmarie Hordern at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pimco Likes Rates Where They Are, CEO Roman Says
item.description: Pimco CEO Emmanuel Roman says, “the moment that we get to a better outcome in the Middle East, you’ll see a release of the bond market and rates to go down.” Roman also sees inflation and the inflation shock as “somehow transitory” in relation to what’s happening in the Middle East. He speaks with David Gura at the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Qatar on Diplomacy and Global Growth
item.description: H.E. Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Prime Minister & Minister of Foreign Affairs for the State of Qatar discusses diplomacy, capital and global growth with Bloomberg’s Mishal Husain at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Aliko Dangote on Investing in Africa
item.description: Dangote Industries President and Chief Executive Aliko Dangote discusses business, investment and Africa’s economic outlook with Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 9/20/2026
item.description: CNN Senior National Security Reporter Jennifer Hansler, Qatar Airways Group CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater, Marsh CEO John Doyle, Oaktree Capital Management Co-Chair Howard Marks, Advisor to the Prime Minister of Qatar and Official Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Dr. Majed Al Ansari, Franklin Templeton Investments CEO Jenny Johnson, Former US Treasury Secretary and Liberty Strategic Capital Founder & Managing Partner Steven Mnuchin, State Street Global Advisors President and CEO Yie-Hsin Hung, Governor and Qatar Central Bank Chairman H.E. Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani and General Atlantic CEO Bill Ford at the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IMF MD on the Global Economic Outlook
item.description: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva discusses the global economic outlook with Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hormuz ‘Cannot Be Obsolete,’ Qatar Energy Minister Says
item.description: Qatar Energy Minister Saad al-Kaabi discusses the future of the Strait of Hormuz and says that to call the strait obsolete is “wrong.” US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent commented on Sept. 1 that the Strait of Hormuz will be like a worthless piece of water in two years. He spoke with Annmarie Hordern at the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Qatar, Brookfield on Trade, Investment and Competition
item.description: H.E. Sheikh Faisal bin Thani bin Faisal Al-Thani, Minister of Commerce & Industry for the State of Qatar and Brookfield CEO Bruce Flatt discuss trade, investment and global competition with Bloomberg’s Christina Ruffini at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: QIA, Apollo & Goldman CEOs on Global Capital
item.description: Mohammed Saif Al-Sowaidi, CEO of QIA, Marc Rowan, Co-founder, Chairman & CEO of Apollo Global Management and David M. Solomon, Chairman & CEO of Goldman Sachs Group discuss where global capital is moving and how investors are positioning for growth with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How India Turned Cricket Into A Billion Dollar Business
item.description: India’s obsession with cricket has helped turn the Indian Premier League into one of the world’s most valuable sports leagues, attracting foreign investors like Blackstone. With only 10 teams serving a country of roughly 1.5 billion people, investors see scarcity, rising media consumption and India’s economic growth as powerful drivers of team valuations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Qatar, Citi and PIMCO on Capital Discipline and Resilience
item.description: H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al-Kuwari, Minister of Finance for the State of Qatar, Jane Fraser, Chair & CEO at Citi and Emmanuel Roman, CEO at PIMCO, discuss fiscal discipline, capital and economic resilience with Bloomberg’s David Gura at the Qatar Economic Forum UNGA Special Edition in New York in 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: General Atlantic CEO Sees Long-Term AI Opportunity
item.description:
General Atlantic CEO Bill Ford says accelerating innovation and entrepreneurship have created one of the strongest environments for growth investing in his three decades in the business, with opportunities spanning the US, Middle East, Asia and Latin America. Ford tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that geopolitical risks are reshaping global supply chains but not reversing globalization, while AI should continue creating investment opportunities despite periods of overvaluation and concerns about safety.
At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why India’s Big Tech Companies Are Betting on Hyderabad
item.description: Hyderabad has spent decades building the talent, infrastructure and business climate to compete with Bangalore, attracting major tech firms while becoming a hub for life sciences. But AI now threatens some of the lower-cost IT work that helped fuel its rise. The test is whether Hyderabad can use its talent base to move from supporting global innovation to creating more of its own. This version corrects a map of India. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Qatar Says LNG Damage May Take Years to Repair
item.description:
Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Qatar Central Bank Governor and Qatar Investment Authority Chairman Sheikh Bandar bin Mohammed bin Saoud Al-Thani says damage to the country’s LNG facilities could take two to three years to repair, with the conflict contributing to a 7% economic contraction even as the non-hydrocarbon economy grows. He says Qatar’s strong fiscal position has allowed QIA to continue investing globally, with technology and AI among its major areas of focus, while the central bank is deploying AI across its own operations.
At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: State Street Sees Resilience Driving Portfolios
item.description:
State Street Investment Management CEO Yie-Hsin Hung says investors have entered an era where resilient portfolios are increasingly important as higher capital costs, geopolitical tensions and technological change create a wider range of potential outcomes. Hung tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that institutional investors are adding liquidity and other portfolio buffers, while State Street is also expanding access to private markets and providing the default ETF for the US government's Trump Accounts program.
At the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Yen Vulnerable With Japan on Holiday After BOJ Disappoints
item.description: The yen is vulnerable to sharp moves and further declines over the next week, with a three-day holiday in Japan set to reduce trading liquidity and investors disappointed that the central bank didn’t offer stronger guidance on the pace of future interest rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Hideyuki Sano and Umesh Desai

item.title: Wall Street Week | India’s Growth Test, Bangalore’s Infrastructure Problem, Cricket Attracts Capital
item.description: This week, a special edition of Wall Street Week from the fastest growing large economy in the world: India. The country's technology sector has helped power its growth, but its success has led to uneven progress that could turn its strengths into weaknesses. Bangalore became India’s tech capital by attracting global investment and growing a deep talent pool, but infrastructure and policies to support the expansion have struggled to keep up. Plus, can Hyderabad overtake Bangalore as India’s leading tech city? Later, Blackstone’s investment in Royal Challengers Bengaluru reflects just how much potential India’s sports and entertainment economy has. This version corrects a map of India. (Source: Bloomberg)
